Docs/Getting started

Getting started

Check artifact availability, prepare the research runtime, and create a registered stage environment.

Before running an example

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

A usable research setup needs the DexArena task and robot modules, object and workstation assets, a compatible ManiSkill/SAPIEN runtime, and a working renderer. Native kitchen evaluation also needs the corresponding RoboCasa scene assets. Policy training adds its own dataset, model and accelerator requirements.

Use the dependency versions and asset layout associated with your research revision. There is no verified public pip install dexarena distribution or one-command asset installer documented here. A generic ManiSkill installation alone does not register the DexArena tasks.

Identify the checkout you have

git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
git ls-files task utils train data_gen

Run these read-only checks in the research checkout. Preserve the commit identifier and local changes with your experiment manifest. If the module directories are absent, the Python examples below cannot run from that checkout; the public repository's current README and license are not a simulator package.

Keep the runtime environment and robot/task assets together with the source revision used for data collection. Changing task geometry, controller settings or joint definitions can invalidate stored demonstrations.

Create one canonical stage

The registry supplies the robot and horizon. This example uses the mouse-clicking stage; it does not assume that every task shares its robot or episode length.

import gymnasium as gym
import task  # Registers the research tasks and robot agents.
from utils.dex_scene_eval import registered_task_settings

env_id = "SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1"
settings = registered_task_settings(env_id)
print(settings)

env = gym.make(
    env_id,
    **settings,
    num_envs=1,
    obs_mode="state",
    sim_backend="physx_cpu",
)
try:
    obs, info = env.reset(seed=10001)
    print(env.action_space)
    print(env.observation_space)
finally:
    env.close()

registered_task_settings resolves the canonical stage robot, pd_joint_pos controller and registered time limit without constructing a simulator. It accepts the 30 canonical subtasks; use the task registry for complete-sequence environments. A state observation is useful for checking registration. Image policies need their documented camera and preprocessing contract.

Choose a formal target

task/config/collection_targets.py lists LONG_TASKS, SUBTASKS and the combined 40 collection targets. The broader Gym registry also contains legacy aliases, retired curricula and variants that are not formal benchmark targets. Enumerating every registered environment will overcount the benchmark.

utils/dex_tasks.py records task instructions and policy metadata. Use the catalog to select the stage, then verify its exact environment ID against these registries. Read the environment's spaces instead of copying another stage's observation width.

Run the first check

Continue with Configurations and Quick evaluation. A successful reset verifies the environment wiring; a learned policy still needs the correct model dependencies, checkpoint and adapter.
